official_sources.title: Practice guide 40 supplement 4: boundary agreements and determined boundaries
Guidance for preparing plans for HM Land Registry applications

verified_facts: a determined boundary records an exact line unlike a general boundary
the determined-boundary plan must identify start end and turning points
the plan must show enough surrounding detail to identify the position on OS mapping
the plan must state its scale
preferred determined-boundary scale is no smaller than 1:200
measurement-based determined boundaries require measurements accurate to plus or minus 10mm
measurements must be horizontal rather than slope distance
measurements must use at least two defined permanent physical reference points
permanent reference features should reasonably remain for at least 10 years
natural growth or decay features are not acceptable permanent references
application plans should avoid disclaimers that cast doubt on scale or accuracy
quality_effect: Separates exact determined-boundary survey evidence from ordinary title-plan geometry and enforces the HM Land Registry measurement-plan requirements before precision promotion.
